candidates.label: location

Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: containedInPlace

candidates.label: containedIn

Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: itemLocation
candidates.comment: A physical location relation between an archive component and its current place, postal address, or textual description of location. Also called current location, item whereabouts, storage location, physical location. Examples: An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Shelf 3, Box 12'. An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Library Basement'. An archive component has an itemLocation of '123 Main St, Anytown'.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: repeatCount

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". candidates.label: recordedIn

candidates.label: source

candidates.label: eventStatus

candidates.label: about

candidates.label: greaterOrEqual

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription

candidates.comment: A classification of a medical condition by its applicable stage. Also called "condition stage", "disease stage", "progression stage". Examples: "The cancer has stage Stage III", "The medical condition's stage is early", "This disease is in stage 2."

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: availability
candidates.comment: The current status of an item's availability for demand or offer. Also called: stock status, item status, product availability. Examples: "Offer 'Product X' availability 'InStock'", "Demand 'Service Y' availability 'OutOfStock'", "Offer 'Limited Edition' availability 'PreOrder'."

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: option
candidates.comment: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: suggestedMinAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the minimum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "minimum age", "lower age limit", "age floor". Examples: "The game has suggestedMinAge 7", "The audience specification includes suggestedMinAge 18", "This content is suitable from suggestedMinAge 3.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMaxAge, which specifies only the maximum.

candidates.label: offers
candidates.comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

chosen_property.label: replacer
chosen_property.justification: The 'replacer' property is a direct and appropriate fit for indicating what the subject (a rejected proposal) is exchanged for or substituted by (a resilience strategy).

candidates.label: replacee
candidates.comment: A replacee relation between a replace action and the entity that is being substituted. Also called item replaced, old item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacee 'old battery'.", "A document update replaces 'version 1.0'.", "A software upgrade replaces 'legacy system'.". Distinct from replacer, which is the entity doing the replacing.

candidates.label: replacer
candidates.comment: A replacer relation between a replace action and the entity that performs the substitution. Also called new item, replacement item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacer 'new battery'.", "A document update uses a replacer 'version 2.0'.", "A software upgrade uses a replacer 'modern system'.". Distinct from replacee, which is the entity being replaced.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: legislationChanges
candidates.comment: A legislative alteration relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it modifies, replaces, corrects, or repeals. Also called alters law, modifies statute, replaces act, repeals legislation. Examples: Legislation X legislationChanges 'Legislation Y'. The new regulation legislationChanges 'several existing laws'. This amendment legislationChanges 'the previous version of the act'. Distinct from legislationAmends, which is a specific type of change (introducing legal changes), and legislationConsolidates, which is about creating a consolidated version.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: currentExchangeRate
candidates.comment: A value relation between an exchange rate specification and the current price of a currency. Also called: exchange value, currency rate, conversion rate. Examples: "USD to EUR" current exchange rate "0.92 EUR per USD", "GBP to JPY" current exchange rate "180 JPY per GBP".

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: correction
candidates.comment: A modification relation between a creative work and the comment, text, or document detailing a correction to it. Also called: erratum, amendment, revision, fix. Examples: "News Article" correction "Editor's Note: A previous version of this article misstated...", "Software Manual" correction "See errata sheet for updates.", "Research Paper" correction "Correction published in Vol. 15, Issue 3.".

candidates.label: option
candidates.comment: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.
